Shared Hosting vs VPS Hosting: Which One Do You Need in Pakistan? (2026)

By ZedgeHost Team · 20 November 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: shared hosting from Rs 1,499 per year fits most small websites in Pakistan: a business site, a blog or a portfolio. VPS hosting from Rs 1,699 per month fits websites that need dedicated resources and full control: a growing online store, several websites on one server, or an application you manage yourself. If you are unsure, start with shared hosting and move to a VPS later with free migration.

Shared hosting vs VPS at a glance

What changesShared hostingVPS hosting
Starts atRs 1,499 per yearRs 1,699 per month
ResourcesShared with other websites on the same serverDedicated CPU, RAM and storage for your server alone
ControlManaged through cPanel; the host runs the serverFull root access; you run the server yourself
Best forSmall business sites, blogs, portfolios, small storesGrowing stores, several websites, agencies, developers
SetupReady to use; upload your site and go liveChoose a location and operating system at checkout, then configure it

What shared hosting actually gives you

On shared hosting, your website runs on a server shared with other websites, and ZedgeHost manages that server for you. You work through cPanel: create email accounts, install WordPress in one click, manage files and databases, and check backups. You never touch the server itself, which is why shared hosting is the simplest way to get a website online. Every shared and WordPress plan includes a free SSL certificate, free cPanel, weekly backups, free website migration and 24/7 support, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. For a full breakdown of what hosting costs in Pakistan, see how much web hosting costs in Pakistan.

Enterprise is currently Rs 4,999 per year, reduced from Rs 9,999. WordPress hosting uses the same four plans and prices as shared hosting, with one-click WordPress installs. If your site grows past what shared hosting handles, cloud hosting from Rs 9,999 per year is the middle step before a server of your own.

What VPS hosting actually gives you

On a VPS, you get your own virtual server with resources reserved for you alone: a set amount of CPU, RAM, storage and data transfer that no other customer can use. You get full root access, a server management panel and VNC access, and you choose the server location (New Jersey, Los Angeles or Dallas) and the operating system (AlmaLinux, Ubuntu, Debian, or an empty disk) at checkout. That control is the whole point of a VPS: you install what you need, configure it your way, and host several websites or applications on one server.

VPS plans are billed monthly, with a yearly option at checkout, and every plan includes an up to 10 Gbps shared port. The trade-off is responsibility: with root access comes server management, so a VPS suits buyers who are comfortable configuring a server, or who have a developer to do it. See the full VPS hosting plans before you decide.

Which one do you need?

A small business website, blog or portfolio

Choose shared hosting. A company profile, a catalogue with photos, an enquiry form and email on your own domain all fit comfortably on a Starter or Standard plan. Shared hosting from Rs 1,499 per year is enough, and if your site is built on WordPress, WordPress hosting from Rs 1,499 per year gives you the same price with one-click installs.

A growing online store or several websites

Choose a VPS when orders and traffic grow, or when you host several websites that need guaranteed resources. A store doing steady daily orders, a site with heavy images or video, or five or ten client sites on one account all point toward VPS hosting from Rs 1,699 per month. If you want more room without managing a server yourself, cloud hosting from Rs 9,999 per year sits in between.

An agency or developer hosting client sites

Choose a VPS. Each client site gets dedicated resources, and you keep full control of the server: the operating system, the software, the security setup and the backups. Start with VPS Basic and scale up only when the sites you host demand it. If you are comparing prices first, see cheap web hosting in Pakistan for the full price picture across shared, cloud and VPS.

What stays the same on both

Whichever you choose, you pay in PKR: Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast or bank transfer, with no international card and no currency conversion. See how to pay with JazzCash or Easypaisa for the steps. Both come with 24/7 support and free website migration if you are moving from another host, and both carry a 30-day money-back guarantee. See how ordering works before you buy, so you know each step from choosing a plan to your website going live.

How to decide in five steps

  1. Start with your real need. One small website fits shared hosting. Several websites, a busy store or full server control points toward a VPS.
  2. Compare the full price, not the headline. Shared hosting is billed per year and VPS per month, so compare the same period: Rs 1,499 per year against Rs 1,699 per month is a real difference, not a small one. Confirm the renewal price too.
  3. Check the resources, not just the price. Count the websites, storage and traffic you actually need. A plan that is too small costs more in moves and upgrades than the saving was worth.
  4. Be honest about control. If you want the host to manage the server, stay on shared hosting with cPanel. If you want root access and your own configuration, a VPS is the right tool.
  5. Know the way out. A 30-day money-back guarantee means you can try the service and leave if it does not fit, and free migration means you can move from shared to VPS later without rebuilding your site.

Ready to get online? Shared hosting starts at Rs 1,499 per year with free SSL, free cPanel, weekly backups, free migration, PKR payments and 24/7 support, and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
